index.casesTitle: In production, not in a pitch deck
index.casesDescription: Projects that real companies run on today, and the services we combined to build them.

faqs.question: Can I hire several services in a single project?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it's the most common case. A custom platform almost always includes integrations, security and handover documentation. Services aren't quoted as separate packages: we build one plan with one team.

faqs.question: How much does a project cost?
faqs.answer: It depends on scope, which is why we don't publish fixed prices. You can get an estimated range in minutes with our [estimator](/en/cotizador), and after a discovery call we deliver a fixed quote with dates.

faqs.question: Can you take over a system built by another vendor?
faqs.answer: Yes. We start with a code and data audit to decide what to keep, what to refactor and what's worth replacing. If the system has become hard-to-maintain legacy, we migrate it in phases without stopping operations, see [legacy system migration](/en/servicios/migracion-datos-legacy).

faqs.question: Do you work alongside our in-house engineering team?
faqs.answer: Yes. Repositories in your name from day one, shared code reviews and documentation written so your team can continue on its own once we're done.

faqs.question: What happens after launch?
faqs.answer: You get a 90-day warranty against any technical failure, at no cost. After that you can stay with us on a maintenance plan or continue with your own team: the code and documentation are already yours.

faqs.question: Which technologies do you use?
faqs.answer: We choose by problem, not by trend. On the web we mostly work with TypeScript, Next.js and React; on mobile, with React Native; on the server, with Node.js and NestJS; and for data, with PostgreSQL. We also know Laravel, PHP and WordPress when the case calls for them. Everything lives in repositories in your name, so you never depend on a proprietary platform of ours.

faqs.question: Do you work with companies outside Colombia?
faqs.answer: Yes. We work with companies in other cities and countries and communicate in English, Spanish and French. Colombia stays on UTC−5 all year with no daylight saving shift, so the gap with your time zone is always the same: none with US Eastern Time in winter, one hour in summer, and six or seven hours with Western Europe. The [estimator](/en/cotizador) shows base prices in US dollars.

faqs.question: How is a project paid for?
faqs.answer: In two payments: 50% at signing, with the agreed schedule, and 50% when you receive the working project, tested end to end and with your final approval. There are no forced monthly fees or recurring licenses.

international.heading: Building for US and UK teams from Bogotá
international.intro: Most of our work for English-speaking clients is done remotely. This is how that works in practice, in plain terms.

items.title: Time zone overlap
items.text: Colombia is UTC−5 all year with no daylight saving, so working hours overlap fully with US Eastern and mostly with Central and Pacific. Weekly demos and quick questions happen the same day.

items.title: Written English by default
items.text: Proposals, technical documentation, pull-request notes and weekly updates are written in English, so the people who will maintain the software can read everything we hand over.

items.title: A price you can plan with
items.text: Reference prices are published in USD on the [project estimator](/en/cotizador) before you ever talk to us, with the scope each figure covers.

items.title: Code you own
items.text: The repository, documentation and infrastructure access are transferred to you at delivery, so you are never locked in to us as a vendor.
